name: The Hollow Vale / Tharion Cycle public reference pack
source_policy: Compact paraphrase and structured provenance only; no wholesale source prose or image mirroring.

world.name: Tharion / The Hollow Vale
world.summary: A mythic Romano-British setting in which memory, naming, silence, magic and unstable geography are part of the world's causal texture. The public wiki presents shifting roads, disappearing names and uncertain time as recurring features.

characters.name: Caelwyn
characters.summary: A central figure tied to the Bell, memory and the Wyrd. The public lore deliberately preserves several incompatible or semi-compatible origin traditions rather than resolving them into one history.

groups.name: Daughters of Avalon
groups.summary: Veiled figures associated with dreams, moonlight, the edges of reality and guidance through the Vale. Their ritual songs are presented as affecting the Wyrd and linking multiple times.

places.name: Elderglen
places.summary: Settlement on the edge of the Vale and the birthplace assigned to Caelwyn in the most grounded origin tradition.

places.name: Tor Velden
places.summary: Sacred hill associated with prophecy, resonance and the Starforged Bell.

artefacts.name: Rune-Stone
artefacts.summary: A fractured inscribed stone linked to names, memory and fate. The lore treats names as active vessels of identity rather than passive labels.

artefacts.name: Starforged Bell
artefacts.summary: A star-forged relic on Tor Velden that anchors the Wyrd to physical reality. Its resonance can bind names into memory and may also erode or hollow what it names.

languages_and_terms.name: Tharionese
languages_and_terms.summary: A ritual and poetic language associated with circular logic, repetition, mirrored structures, memory anchoring and communication across seen and unseen layers.

languages_and_terms.name: Wyrmreth
languages_and_terms.summary: The spiral model of memory and fate. Public lore describes the Wyrd as non-linear, with past, present and future coiling back through one another.

languages_and_terms.name: Lleirwyn
languages_and_terms.summary: A Tharionese term associated with moonlight and the Daughters of Avalon.

languages_and_terms.name: swefnunga wyrcan
languages_and_terms.summary: Name given to the dream-shaping chants associated with the Daughters of Avalon.

events.name: Elysian Convergence
events.summary: Rare celestial event used by one major Caelwyn birth tradition to explain her manifestation beneath the Wyrm Tree.

events.name: Breaking of the Stars
events.summary: Cosmic event used by the Starborn Nomad origin tradition to explain Caelwyn's descent from a celestial realm.

events.name: Thonbrial aethrun
events.summary: The 'last bell' event associated with fracture, memory disruption and the broken Rune-Stone.

rules.name: Memory is causal
rules.summary: Memory in the Vale acts as a force that can anchor identity, affect reality and bind separate moments rather than functioning only as recollection.

rules.name: Names carry identity and power
rules.summary: Names are repeatedly treated as containers or anchors of identity. Naming, inscription and resonance can therefore alter a person's or thing's continuity.

rules.name: Competing in-world traditions remain live
rules.summary: The public lore explicitly presents multiple versions of Caelwyn's origins. ArcSweep should preserve these as named traditions rather than selecting a single canonical winner.

myth_variants.subject: caelwyn
myth_variants.label: Wyrm Tree / Elysian Convergence
myth_variants.summary: Caelwyn originates beneath the ancient Wyrm Tree during a celestial convergence and is marked by a luminous sign tied to memory prophecy.

myth_variants.subject: caelwyn
myth_variants.label: Starborn Nomad
myth_variants.summary: Caelwyn descends from a celestial realm after the Breaking of the Stars and carries inaccessible memories of that origin.

myth_variants.subject: caelwyn
myth_variants.label: Bell-Touched Wanderer
myth_variants.summary: Caelwyn is an orphan who encounters the Bell in childhood, acquires a connection to the Vale and later adopts the name Caelwyn.

myth_variants.subject: caelwyn
myth_variants.label: Child of the Vale
myth_variants.summary: Caelwyn is born in Elderglen and becomes important through courage, curiosity and her own relationship with the Vale rather than through celestial birth.

provenance.method: web-indexed author-site review plus compact paraphrased extraction
notes: This pack is a reference layer, not an import of Burton's prose.
Contradictory in-world origin traditions are retained as separate variants.
Source URLs remain attached so later ArcSweep reviews can revisit author-site context.
